note: Times are from GK-1 and only a guide: the way out of Delhi can take as long as the road beyond it, and in winter fog closes the expressways at dawn. Where a train is faster, the card says so. Gurugram and Noida are zones, not day trips. Researched, not yet done — rate them as you go.

items.title: Agra and the Taj
items.priceNote: About ₹250 for Indian visitors with the mausoleum; more for foreign ones
items.transit: Gatimaan Express from Hazrat Nizamuddin, under 2 h; about 3 h 30 min by the Yamuna Expressway
items.why: The Taj Mahal is not overrated, and seeing it at sunrise, before the crowd, is how to prove it. Add Agra Fort, where Shah Jahan spent his last years looking across the river at the tomb he built, and Itimad-ud-Daulah, the small marble tomb that came first. At sunset, Mehtab Bagh has the Taj from the far bank. The Taj is shut on Fridays; buy tickets online.

stops.text: The Gatimaan Express from Hazrat Nizamuddin at eight
The Taj Mahal — sunrise if you stay over, otherwise straight from the station
Agra Fort, where Shah Jahan was kept, looking across at the Taj
Itimad-ud-Daulah, the 'baby Taj', across the river
Sunset at Mehtab Bagh, facing the Taj from the far bank

items.season: October to March. Closed Fridays. Full-moon night viewings are held a few nights a month by booking.

items.title: Fatehpur Sikri
items.priceNote: Small ASI fee for the palaces; the mosque is free
items.transit: Yamuna Expressway via Agra, about 4 h
items.why: Akbar's red sandstone capital, built from 1571 and abandoned within fifteen years, forty minutes past Agra. The palaces are empty and intact. The great mosque beside them is anything but: through the Buland Darwaza, a gateway fifty-odd metres high, the white marble tomb of Salim Chishti still draws people tying threads to its screens for a wish. Do it with Agra if you start early, or on its own.

stops.text: The palace courtyards: the Diwan-i-Khas and its carved central pillar
Through the Buland Darwaza to the Jama Masjid
Salim Chishti's marble tomb — tie a thread for a wish
On to Agra if you started early

items.season: October to March; midday in summer is punishing on the red stone.

items.title: Jaipur
items.transit: Trains from New Delhi in about 4 h 30 min; about 5 h on NH48
items.why: Close enough for a weekend, far enough to feel like somewhere else. Amber Fort in the morning, before the heat and the coaches. The City Palace and the stone instruments of Jantar Mantar, which still tell the time, in the afternoon. Hawa Mahal from a café terrace opposite, and sunset from Nahargarh above the old city. Eat at LMB in Johari Bazaar and shop the bazaars for block prints. The morning trains are calmer than the drive.

stops.text: Amber Fort first thing, before the coaches
Jal Mahal from the road on the way back
The City Palace and Jantar Mantar
Hawa Mahal from a rooftop café opposite
Sunset from Nahargarh, and dinner at LMB in Johari Bazaar

items.season: October to March. The Jaipur Literature Festival is in late January.

items.title: Chand Baori, Abhaneri
items.transit: NH48 and the Dausa road, about 4 h 30 min; an hour and a half short of Jaipur
items.why: A stepwell dug in the ninth century and thirteen storeys deep, three of its sides a geometry of about 3,500 narrow steps down to green water. It sits in a village off the Jaipur–Agra road, and it is the best reason on this map to take the long way to Jaipur. The Harshat Mata temple across the lane is from the same age.

stops.text: Chand Baori, the thirteen-storey stepwell — early, for the shadows
Harshat Mata temple across the lane
On to Jaipur, an hour and a half on

items.title: Neemrana Fort-Palace
items.priceNote: Day pass with a meal; zipline extra
items.why: A fort from 1464 on the Jaipur highway, restored as a hotel and stepped down its hillside in terraces. It is the easy Delhi escape: arrive for lunch, walk the ramparts and the courtyards, and ride the zipline over the fort and the Aravallis. Day visitors buy a pass, usually with a meal; stay the night and the place is quiet after dark.

stops.text: Arrive for lunch on the terraces
The zipline over the fort and the hills
The stepwell in the village below
Sunset from the ramparts, or stay the night

items.title: Sultanpur & Farrukhnagar
items.transit: Past Gurugram on the Farrukhnagar road, about 1 h 30 min
items.why: A shallow lake and scrub woodland on the far side of Gurugram, which from October to March fills with birds that winter here from Central Asia and Siberia: bar-headed geese, pintails, cranes, and flamingos in a good year. Arrive at opening and walk the loop around the water with binoculars. On the way back, stop at Farrukhnagar for the Ghaus Ali Shah baoli, an octagonal Mughal stepwell almost nobody has heard of.

stops.text: Arrive at opening, binoculars ready
The loop round the lake: bar-headed geese, pintails, cranes
Farrukhnagar on the way back for the Ghaus Ali Shah baoli

items.season: Mid-October to March for the migrants; it is dry and empty in summer.

items.title: Keoladeo, Bharatpur
items.priceNote: Entry fee, plus the rickshaw or bicycle
items.transit: Yamuna Expressway to Mathura, then west, about 3 h 45 min
items.why: The marsh the Maharajas of Bharatpur kept for duck shoots, now a World Heritage site and one of the best places in Asia to watch birds. Hire a bicycle, or a cycle rickshaw whose driver has been trained by the park as a guide, and go slowly along the causeways between the water: painted storks, pelicans, owls, and in winter the migrants. November to February is the season. An easy pairing with Mathura or Agra.

stops.text: Hire a bicycle, or a trained rickshaw-guide, at the gate
The main causeway past the painted stork colonies
Ask the guide for the owls and the pythons
On to Agra or Mathura

items.season: November to February for the migrants; the storks nest from August to October.

items.title: Mathura & Vrindavan
items.why: Krishna's country, three hours down the Yamuna Expressway. Mathura has the temple on his birthplace; Vrindavan, a few kilometres on, has thousands more, and the one everybody goes to is Banke Bihari, where the curtain before the image is drawn shut every few minutes so no one looks too long. In March the villages around them hold the most famous Holi in India, Barsana's Lathmar Holi, with sticks. The crowds are the point here; go knowing that.

stops.text: Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura
Banke Bihari in Vrindavan — the curtain opens and shuts
Keshi Ghat on the Yamuna at dusk for the aarti
Lassi and peda in the lanes

items.season: October to March; Holi in March and Janmashtami in August are unforgettable and overwhelming.

items.title: Haridwar & Rishikesh
items.priceNote: Free to wander; rafting from a few hundred rupees
items.transit: Trains to Haridwar in about 4 h 30 min; 5 h 30 min by road
items.why: The Ganga coming out of the hills. Haridwar has the evening aarti at Har Ki Pauri: fire, bells, and thousands on the ghats. Rishikesh, forty minutes further, has the bridges, the ashrams, the cafés, and rafting on the river from about September to June. The ashram where the Beatles stayed in 1968 is a painted ruin you can walk through. Take the train to Haridwar and skip the drive.

stops.text: The morning Shatabdi to Haridwar
The evening aarti at Har Ki Pauri
Next day, Rishikesh: walk across the Ram Jhula bridge
The Beatles Ashram, painted and ruined, in Rajaji park
Rafting on the Ganga, September to June

items.season: September to November and February to April. Rafting stops in the monsoon.

items.title: Landour
items.transit: Train to Dehradun and a taxi up, or about 7 h by road
items.why: Above Mussoorie, and nothing like it: a quiet cantonment of old cottages and deodar forest, with a road that loops the top of the hill in an hour's walk. Have pancakes at Char Dukan, buy jam and peanut butter at Prakash Stores, and read Ruskin Bond, who has written about this hill for half a century. A long weekend, not a day.

stops.text: Train to Dehradun, taxi up the hill
Pancakes at Char Dukan
The Chakkar loop round the top of the hill, through the deodars
Jam and peanut butter at Prakash Stores
Cambridge Book Depot on the Mall in Mussoorie, for Ruskin Bond

items.season: October and November are clearest for the Himalaya; spring for the rhododendrons. Avoid the summer crowds.

items.title: Chandigarh
items.priceNote: Small fees; the Capitol Complex by booking
items.transit: Shatabdi from New Delhi in about 3 h 30 min; about 4 h 30 min on NH44
items.why: The city Le Corbusier planned in the 1950s, and still the best argument for it anywhere in India. The Capitol Complex, with the High Court, the Secretariat, the Assembly and the Open Hand, is a World Heritage site; book a guided visit. Then Nek Chand's Rock Garden, forty acres of figures he built in secret from broken crockery, bangles and rubble, and a walk round Sukhna Lake.

stops.text: The morning Shatabdi
The Capitol Complex by guided tour — book, and bring ID
Nek Chand's Rock Garden
Sukhna Lake at sunset
Dinner in Sector 17 before the train back

items.title: Sariska & Bhangarh
items.why: A tiger reserve in the Aravallis that came back: by 2005 every tiger here had been poached, and the ones there now were brought in from Ranthambore. Book a jeep safari at dawn. On the far edge of the reserve, Bhangarh is a ruined seventeenth-century town with its bazaar, temples and palace still standing in outline, called the most haunted place in India. The Archaeological Survey locks it at sunset.

stops.text: A dawn jeep safari, booked
Bhangarh, the ruined town, in the afternoon — locked at sunset
Alwar City Palace on the way back

items.season: October to June; the park closes to safaris in the monsoon.

items.title: Mangar Bani
items.why: The last sacred grove of the Delhi ridge, an hour from GK on the Gurugram–Faridabad road. The villagers of Mangar have protected it for generations as the forest of a local saint, and it is one of the few places left with the old dhau woodland of the Aravallis. Walk the trails early, before the heat, and bring water: there is nothing to buy.

stops.text: Start at dawn from Mangar village
The grove trails through the dhau forest
The ridge above for the view over the Aravallis
Chai in the village on the way out

items.season: October to March, early mornings only. There is no water on the trail.

items.title: Amritsar and the Golden Temple
items.priceNote: The temple and its kitchen are free; the border ceremony is free
items.transit: The Shatabdi from New Delhi, about 6 h — a weekend
items.why: The holiest place of the Sikhs, a gilded temple in a pool of water that is open to everybody, day and night, and whose kitchen feeds tens of thousands of people a day for free, at the same floor, whoever they are. See it at night when it glows, and at dawn when the holy book is carried in. Then the kulcha, and the flag ceremony at the Pakistan border.
items.hoursNote: A place to spend the day, not a door — what is in it keeps its own hours

stops.text: The Golden Temple at night: cover your head, leave your shoes, walk the marble around the pool
Sit on the floor for langar in the free kitchen — and help with the dishes if you like
Jallianwala Bagh, a few minutes away, and the Partition Museum in the Town Hall
Amritsari kulcha for lunch in the old city
The Beating Retreat at the Attari–Wagah border, an hour out, in the late afternoon

items.season: October to March. Summers are over 40°C. The temple is at its most beautiful on Gurpurab and Diwali.

items.title: Jim Corbett National Park
items.priceNote: Jeep safaris by booking; lodging is the cost
items.transit: About 6 h by road to Ramnagar; trains run overnight to Ramnagar
items.why: India's oldest national park, founded in 1936, in the Himalayan foothills along the Ramganga river, with one of the densest tiger populations anywhere. You go on jeep safaris at dawn and dusk into sal forest and grassland, and see elephants, deer, crocodiles and, with luck, a tiger. Book safaris on the official site when they open, weeks ahead.
items.hoursNote: A place to spend the day, not a door — what is in it keeps its own hours

stops.text: A dawn jeep safari from Ramnagar — book the zone ahead
Dhikala, deep in the park, for elephants on the grassland (from mid-November)
The Ramganga at Garjia temple on its rock in the river
An afternoon safari in a second zone

items.season: Most zones open 15 October; Dhikala from 15 November; the core closes in the monsoon. Winter mornings are cold — bring layers.

items.title: Ranthambore
items.priceNote: Safaris by booking; lodging is the cost
items.transit: Trains to Sawai Madhopur in about 5 h — a weekend
items.why: The place tigers are photographed from a few metres away, lying in the ruins of a thousand-year-old fort on a hill in the middle of the jungle. The park is dry deciduous forest with lakes and old pavilions, and its tigers are famously unbothered by jeeps. Take the train, book two safaris, and climb the fort.
items.hoursNote: A place to spend the day, not a door — what is in it keeps its own hours

stops.text: Train to Sawai Madhopur
A dawn safari by gypsy — book the zone on the forest department site
Ranthambore Fort, a World Heritage site, and the Ganesh temple at its top
An afternoon safari
Dastkar, the women's craft project on the park road

items.season: October to June; the core zones close in the monsoon. The hot months, April to June, are best for sightings and hardest to bear.

items.title: Shimla by the toy train
items.priceNote: The toy train is cheap; book seats ahead
items.transit: Shatabdi to Kalka, about 4 h, then the narrow-gauge train up, about 5 h — a weekend
items.why: The summer capital of the Raj, reached the old way: the Kalka–Shimla railway, a World Heritage narrow-gauge line from 1903 that climbs through more than a hundred tunnels and over arched bridges into the pines. It takes five hours to go ninety-six kilometres, and that is the point. At the top, the Mall, Christ Church and the monkeys of Jakhu.
items.hoursNote: A place to spend the day, not a door — what is in it keeps its own hours

stops.text: The early Shatabdi to Kalka
The toy train up: sit on the valley side, and change at Barog for breakfast
The Mall and the Ridge, and Christ Church at dusk
Next morning, up to Jakhu temple — hold on to your glasses
The Viceregal Lodge, now the Institute of Advanced Study, by tour

items.season: October and November are clear and cool; December to February can bring snow. Avoid May and June, when the hill is packed.
